claim: A toy RAG agent evaluated with a 0.5 keyword-overlap threshold reported 100% 'accuracy' while the same answers scored only 0.04 average BLEU and 0.24 average F1, demonstrating that naive keyword-match accuracy metrics can drastically overstate agent output quality compared to n-gram or precision/recall-based metrics.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — rigid evals must use stricter metrics than keyword overlap, since lenient thresholds mask low-quality output
scope_conditions: single toy LangChain + IBM Granite RAG agent, 4 test queries on The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes text
quoted_support: Total Entries: 4, Accurate Entries: 4 (100.00%), Average BLEU Score: 0.04, Average F1 Score: 0.24

claim: A production perinatal-care AI platform (MyLUA Health) built on IBM watsonx.ai, watsonx Orchestrate, Granite models, and RAG reports that 79% of users felt comfortable sharing sensitive health information with the platform, attributed to grounded, governed, HIPAA-compliant agent responses.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — grounding (RAG) plus governance can measurably increase user trust in regulated domains
scope_conditions: single vendor case study, healthcare domain, no independent verification
quoted_support: The result: 79% of users felt comfortable sharing sensitive health information with the platform, a direct outcome of accurate, governed, agent-driven responses rather than generic answers.
numbers: 79% of users comfortable sharing sensitive health info

claim: A four-component framework (Profile, Memory, Planning, Action) is proposed as the standard architecture for LLM-based autonomous agents, where Memory can be unified or hybrid and Planning can follow predefined steps or adapt dynamically via feedback.
stance_target: Triggers/Infrastructure pillar — foundational vocabulary for describing single-agent architecture components that scale into multi-agent Director/Worker systems
quoted_support: The framework presented in figure-1 provides a holistic design for large language model (LLM)-based autonomous agents, emphasizing the interplay between key components: profile, memory, planning and action.
